name: Darin Balaban
statement:
I'm Darin Balaban, a painter and muralist based in Sebastopol, California. For over a decade I've painted large-scale murals in a signature geometric abstraction — bold color, interlocking shapes, and pattern systems built piece by piece the way you'd build a structure. It's a visual language people recognize on sight, and it's made for exactly the kind of wall NewBo City Market has: big, public, and seen every day by the whole community.

My recent work includes the stacked-container mural at Rolling Loud 2025 in Inglewood and the Acrosports gymnasium wall in San Francisco — a 15-by-45-foot interior mural, which is the closest cousin to this project: a large interior wall in a busy public building, painted to energize the room without overwhelming what happens in it. I've also painted at the Plaza Walls festival in Oklahoma City and on commissions for property owners, developers, and businesses, including Waterbar and Epic Steakhouse in San Francisco.

What draws me to this wall is the brief itself: honor where a neighborhood comes from and where it's going, in the same image. My pattern systems do that naturally — older rhythms and new ones interlocked in a single field of color, so the history reads as the structure the present is built on. I work collaboratively by default: festival walls are painted in front of crowds, and my commissioned work is developed with owners and committees, with design review built into the process. I'd welcome the chance to build the design with your committee the same way.
